memory_update.text: LW is the primary US-listed direct frozen potato / French fry processor for this node; keep as reference/direct-exposure anchor.
JBTM is a strong underfollowed equipment-lane candidate because potato processors need industrial frying, freezing, filtration, and automation systems to deliver consistent fries at scale.
LNN is a speculative-shadow candidate tied to potato crop water reliability and irrigation technology; needs proof of meaningful processing-potato grower exposure.
BG is a second-order fry-oil input candidate; relevant to restaurant fry consistency but too diversified to treat as a pure frozen-potato chokepoint without more segment/customer evidence.

The frozen-fries chokepoint should be decomposed into processor capacity, processing-grade potato supply, industrial fry/freezer equipment, oil/filtration inputs, and foodservice distribution reliability.
Private leaders McCain, J.R. Simplot, Cavendish, Ventura Foods, and Golden State Foods appear important but are not US-listed common-equity candidates; use them as customer/supplier map context only.

node: Frozen potato products and French fry supply
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the frozen potato / French fry node found one direct public processor, one food-processing equipment vendor, one irrigation/crop-capacity infrastructure provider, and one fry-oil input supplier. The strongest direct public-market mapping is Lamb Weston. The best underfollowed chokepoint-adjacent mapping is JBT Marel, because commercial fry plants depend on high-volume frying, freezing, filtration, and automation systems. Lindsay and Bunge are included as second-order hypotheses tied to raw potato crop reliability and fry-oil consistency, respectively. No buy/sell view is implied.
